G3500.def:
νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ 
(νεκρόω), 
__1. a putting to death. 
__2. a state of death, death: Romains 4:19, 2 Corinthiens 4:10 (see Deiss., LAE, 94).†

G3501.def:
νέος, -α, -ον 
[in LXX for נַעַר (Genèse 37:2, Exo_33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Lévitique 23:16, Nombres 28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטָן, צָעִיר, etc. ;] 
__1. young, youthful: Tite 2:4. 
__2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Matthieu 26:20), Matthieu 9:17, Marc 2:22, Luc 5:37-39; φύραμα (figuratively), 1 Corinthiens 5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., Hébreux 9:15), Hébreux 12:24; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Éphésiens 2:15), Colossiens 3:10. 
__3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Luc 15:12-13 22:26, Jean 21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Actes 5:6 (Rackham, in l), 1 Timothée 5:11, Tite 2:6; opposite to πρεσβύτεροι, 1 Timothée 5:1, 1 Pierre 5:5; αἱ ν., 1 Timothée 5:2 5:14. 
__4. Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: Actes 16:11 (Rec., Νεάπολις, which see) 
νεώτερος, see: νέος 
SYN.: καινός, which see

G3502.def:
νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att.. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ 
(νόος), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן ;] 
a young bird: Luc 2:24 (LXX).†

G3503.def:
νεότης, -ητος, ἡ
(νέος), [in LXX chiefly for נָעוּר ;] 
youth: Marc 10:20, Luc 18:21, Actes 26:4, 1 Timothée 4:12.†

G3504.def:
νεό-φυτος, -ον
(νέος, φύω) [in LXX: Job 14:9, Psaumes 144:12, Ésaïe 5:7 (נֶטַע), Psaumes 128:3 (שְׁתִל)* ;] 
newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1 Timothée 3:6†

G3506.def:
νεύω 
[in LXX: Proverbes 4:5 21:1 * ;] 
to nod or beckon, as a sign : with dative of person(s) and inf., Jean 13:24, Actes 24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).†

G3507.def:
νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ
(νέφος), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָן, also for עָב, etc. ;] 
a cloud (single and specific as opposite to νεφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): Matthieu 17:5 24:30 26:64, Marc 9:7 13:26 14:62, Luc 9:34-35 12:54 21:37, Actes 1:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:17, Ju 12, Apocalypse 1:7 10:1 11:12 14:14-16; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness (Exode 14:19-20, Psaumes 105:39, al.): 1 Corinthiens 10:1-2.†

G3508.def:
Νεφθαλείμ
(-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ 
indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי)
Naphtali: Matthieu 4:13, 15" (LXX) Apocalypse 7:6.†

G3509.def:
νέφος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנַן ;] 
a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: Hébreux 12:1.†

G3510.def:
νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX for כִּלְיָה, Exode 29:13, al.; metaphorically, Psaumes 7:9 16:7 26:2, Wis.1:6, al. ;] 
a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaphorically, of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Apocalypse 2:23.†

G3511.def:
νεω-κόρος, -ου 
a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (see DB, i, 722 b) : Actes 19:35.†

G3512.def:
νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν
(νεώτερος), [in LXX: 3Ma.4:8 * ;] 
= νεανικός, 
youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, 2 Timothée 2:22 (Polyb.).†

G3513.def:
νή 
particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: see τ. ὑγίειαν, Genèse 42:15-16 (חַי) * ;] 
by: with accusative, 1 Corinthiens 15:31.†

G3514.def:
νήθω 
[in LXX for טָוָה, שָׁזַר hoph., Exode 26:31 35:25, al. ;] 
to spin: Matthieu 6:28, Luc 12:27.†

G3515.def:
νηπιάζω 
(νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.) 
to be a babe: 1 Corinthiens 14:20.†

G3516.def:
νήπιος, -α, -ον 
[in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי, etc. ;] 
infant; of children and minors: Matthieu 21:16 (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 13:11, Galates 4:1 (see Lft., in l). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple (Psaumes 19:8, Proverbes 1:32 al.): Matthieu 11:25, Luc 10:21, Romains 2:20, Galates 4:3, Éphésiens 4:14, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:7 (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, Hébreux 5:13; ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, 1 Corinthiens 3:1.†

G3517.def: Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)

G3518.def:
Νηρεί (Rec. -ρί), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֵרִיָּה), 
Neri: Luc 3:27.†

G3519.def:
νησίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.) 
a small island: Actes 27:16.†

G3520.def:
νῆσος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for אִי ;] 
an island: Actes 13:6 27:26 28:1, 7 28:9, 11 Apocalypse 1:9 6:14 16:20.†

G3522.def:
νηστεύω
(νῆστις), [in LXX for צוּם ;] 
to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): Matthieu 4:2 6:16-18 9:14-15 Marc 2:18-20, Luc 5:33-35 18:12, Actes 13:2-3.†

G3523.def:
νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ
(νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω), 
in cl., chiefly poët., 
[in LXX: Dan LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)* ;] 
not eating, fasting: Matthieu 15:32, Marc 8:3.†

G3524.def:
νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον), 
(νήφω), 
__1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine. 
__2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: 1 Timothée 3:2 3:11, Tite 2:2.†

G3525.def:
νήφω 
to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1 Thessaloniciens 5:6 5:8, 2 Timothée 4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1 Pierre 1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).†
SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω

G3528.def:
νικἀω, -ῶ
(νίκη), [in LXX: Psaumes 51:4 (זָכָה), Proverbes 6:25 frequently (חָמַד); in 4Mac ;] 
to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, Apocalypse 3:21 6:2; C. inf., Apocalypse 5:5; of Christians, Apocalypse 2:7, 11 2:17, 26 3:5, 12 3:21 21:7; before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), Apocalypse 15:2; as law-term (cl.), Romains 3:4 (LXX); with accusative of person(s), Luc 11:22, Apocalypse 11:7 13:7 ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, Jean 16:33 (τ. κόσμον), Apocalypse 17:14; of Christians, 1 Jean 4:4; τ. πονηρόν, 1 Jean 2:13-14; αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ, 1 Jean 2:10), Apocalypse 12:11; with accusative of thing(s), τὸν κόσμον, Jean 16:33, 1 Jean 5:4-5; τὸ κακόν, Romains 12:21; pass., μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τ. κακοῦ, ib. (cf. ὑπερ-νικάω).†

G3529.def:
νίκη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: 1 Chroniques 29:11 (נֶצַח), frequently in 1-4 Mac ;] 
victory: 1 Jean 5:4.†

G3531.def:
Νικολαΐτης, -αυ, ὁ 
a Nicolaitan: pl., Apocalypse 2:6, 15.†

G3533.def:
Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ 
Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l): Tite 3:12†

G3534.def:
νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη, 
[in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Esther 3:9, 2Ma.10:38, 4Ma.17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Job 14:20), 2 Rois 2:26, Job 36:7, Amos 1:11 8:7, Jérémie 3:5, La 5:20 (נֶצַח, as נ֝ in Syr., = victory)* ;] 
victory: Matthieu 12:20 (Ésaïe 42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), 1 Corinthiens 15:54 (Ésaïe 25:8, Aq., Th.), 1 Corinthiens 15:55 (Osée 13:14, LXX δίκη), 1 Corinthiens 15:57.†

G3536.def:
Νινευείτης (Rec. -ενίτης, L, -ΐτης), -ου, ὁ 
a Ninevite: Matthieu 12:41, Luc 11:30, 32.†

G3538.def:
νίπτω late form of νίζω, 
[in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ ;] 
to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), Jean 13:8; τ. πόδας, Jean 13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14, 1 Timothée 5:10; mid., reflexive, 
to wash oneself: Jean 9:7, 11 9:15; τ. χεῖρας, Matthieu 15:2, Marc 7:3; τ. πόδας, Jean 13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Matthieu 6:17 (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).†
νίζω, see: νίπτω 
SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω

G3539.def:
νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ 
(νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;] 
__1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Matthieu 16:9, Marc 8:17; with accusative, Éphésiens 3:4, 1 Timothée 1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jean 12:40; pass., Romains 1:20; before ὅτι, Matthieu 15:17 16:11, Marc 7:18; with accusative and inf., Hébreux 11:8. 
__2. to think, consider: absol., Matthieu 24:15, Marc 13:14, Éphésiens 3:20; with accusative of thing(s), 2 Timothée 2:7 
(cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†

G3540.def:
νόημα, -τος, τό
(νοέω) [in LXX: Sir.21:11, Bar.2:8, 3Ma.5:30 * ;] 
a thought, purpose, design: 2 Corinthiens 2:11 10:5 11:3, Philippiens 4:7. Meton., of the mind, 2 Corinthiens 3:14 4:4.†

G3541.def:
νόθος, -η, -ον 
[in LXX: Wis.4:3 * ;] 
a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: Hébreux 12:8.†

G3542.def:
νομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;] 
__1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jean 10:9 
__2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2 Timothée 2:17 (Polyb.).†

G3543.def:
νομίζω
(νόμος), [in LXX: Wis.13:2 17:3, Sir.29:4, 1-28; 2Ma.4:1-50, 4Ma.8:1-29 * ;] 
__1. to practise, hold by custom: Actes 16:13 (Rec., but see infr.). 
__2. to deem, consider, suppose: Matthieu 5:17 10:34 20:10, Luc 2:44 3:23, Actes 7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29, 1 Corinthiens 7:26 7:36, 1 Timothée 6:5.†
SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v

G3544.def:
νομικός, -ή, -όν
(νόμος), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:4 * ;] 
__1. relating to law: μάχαι, Tite 3:9. 
__2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Matthieu 22:35, Luc 10:25, Tite 3:13; pl., Luc 7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3 (cf. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v

G3545.def:
νομίμως 
adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:18 * ;] 
rightly, lawfully: 1 Timothée 1:8, 2 Timothée 2:5.†

G3546.def:
νόμισμα, -τος, τό
(νομίζω), [in LXX: Esther 8:36 (דָּת), Néhémie 7:71 R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), 1Ma.15:6 * ;] 
__1. that which is established by usage, a custom. 
__2. The current coin of a state: Matthieu 22:19.†

G3547.def:
νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ 
a teacher of the law: Luc 5:17, Actes 5:34, 1 Timothée 1:7 (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v

G3548.def:
νομοθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: 2Ma.6:23, 4Ma.5:35 4Mac 17:16 * ;] 
legislation, lawgiving: Romains 9:4.†

G3549.def:
νομοθετέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX for יָרָה hi. ;] 
__1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: Hébreux 7:11. 
__2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., Hébreux 8:6.†

G3550.def:
νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ
(νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: Psaumes 9:20 * ;] 
a law­giver: Jacques 4:12.†

G3551.def:
νόμος, -ου, ὁ 
(νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc. ;] 
that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.); 
__1. of law in general: Romains 3:27 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, Hébreux 8:10 10:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Galates 6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Jacques 1:25 2:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), Jacques 2:8. 
__2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: Romains 7:21, 23a, 25 8:2. 
__3. Of the Mosaic law: Matthieu 5:18, Luc 2:27, Jean 1:17, Actes 6:13, Romains 2:15, 1 Corinthiens 9:8, 1 Timothée 1:8, Hébreux 7:19; al.; Μωυσέως, Luc 2:22, Jean 7:23, Actes 15:5, al.; κυρίου, Luc 2:39; κατὰ τὸν ν., Actes 22:12, Hébreux 7:5 9:22. 
__4. As printed, Abbott-Smith mistakenly numbers this as 3.Anarthrous (Bl, §46, 8; ICC on Romains 2:12, 13), νόμος, 
__(a) of law in general: Romains 2:12, 14b 3:20, 21 4:15, al.; 
__(b) of the Mosaic law in its quality as law: Romains 2:14a 5:20 10:4, Galates 2:19, al.; οἱ ἐκ ν., Romains 4:14; ὑπὸ νόμον, 1 Corinthiens 9:20, Galates 4:5; ν. πράσσειν (πληροῦν), Romains 2:25 13:8. 
__5. Of Christian teaching: ν. πίστεως, Romains 3:27; τ. Χριστοῦ, Galates 6:2. 
__6. By meton., of the books which contain the law; 
__(a) of the Pentateuch: Matthieu 12:5, Jean 1:45, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ οἱ προφῆται, Matthieu 5:17, Luc 16:16, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ προφῆται κ. ψαλμοί, Luc 24:44. 
__(b) of the OT Scriptures in general (as Heb. תּוֹרָה): Jean 10:34 12:34 15:25, 1 Corinthiens 14:21, al.

G3552.def:
νοσέω, -ῶ
(νόσος), [in LXX (metaphorically): Wis.17:8 * ;] 
to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, 1 Timothée 6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).†

G3554.def:
νόσος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for חֲלִי, etc. ;] 
disease, sickness: Matthieu 4:23-24 8:17 (Aq.) Matthieu 9:35 10:1, Marc 1:34, Luc 4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1, Actes 19:12.†
SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια

G3555.def:
νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(νοσσός), 
late form of cl., νεοσσιά, 
[in LXX chiefly for קֵן ;] 
__1. a nest of birds. 
__2. a brood of young birds: Luc 13:34.†

G3556.def:
νοσσίον, -ου, τό dimin. of νοσσός, which see, 
[in LXX: Psaumes 84:3 (אֶפְרֹחַ) * ;] 
a young bird: Matthieu 23:37.†

G3557.def:
νοσφίζω
(νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: Josué 7:1 (לָקַח), 2Ma.4:32 * ;] 
__1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon. 
__2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tite 2:10 (for ex. in π., see MM, xvii); before ἀπό, Actes 5:2-3.†

G3558G.def:
νότος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;] 
__1. prop., the south wind: Luc 12:55, Actes 27:13 28:13 
__2. South: Luc 13:29, Apocalypse 21:13 
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Matthieu 12:42, Luc 11:31.†

G3558H.def:
νότος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;] 
__1. prop., the south wind: Luc 12:55, Actes 27:13 28:13 
__2. South: Luc 13:29, Apocalypse 21:13 
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Matthieu 12:42, Luc 11:31.†

G3559.def:
νουθεσία, -ας ἡ
(νουθετέω), 
= cl. νουθέτησις 
[in LXX: Wis.6:6 * ;] 
admonition: 1 Corinthiens 10:11, Éphésiens 6:4, Tite 3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).†

G3560.def:
νουθετέω, -ῶ 
(νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: 1 Rois 3:13 (כָּהָה pi.), Job 8:1-22 (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 12:2, 26 * ;] 
to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), Actes 20:31, Romains 15:14, 1 Corinthiens 4:14, Colossiens 1:28 3:16, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:12 5:14, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:15.†

G3561.def:
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ 
(νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;] 
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Colossiens 2:16.†

G3562.def:
νουνεχῶς 
adv. (νοῦς, ἔχω) 
sensibly, discreetly: Marc 12:34.†

G3563.def:
νοῦς
(contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;] 
__1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Romains 7:23): Luc 24:45, Romains 1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5, Éphésiens 4:17, 23 Philippiens 4:7, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:2, 1 Timothée 6:5, 2 Timothée 3:8, Tite 1:15, Apocalypse 13:18 17:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), Colossiens 2:18; opposite to σάρξ, Romains 7:25; to πνεῦμα, 1 Corinthiens 14:14-15; to γλῶσσα, 1 Corinthiens 14:19 
__2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: Romains 11:34 = 1 Corinthiens 2:16" (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 1:10.†
νόος, see: νοῦς 
SYN.: see: πνεῦμα

G3564.def:
Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see), 
Nymphas: Colossiens 4:15, R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).†
Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): Colossiens 4:15, WH, R, mg.†

G3566.def:
νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX for חָתָן ;] 
a bridegroom: Matthieu 9:15 25:1, 5-6 25:10, Marc 2:19-20, Luc 5:34-35, Jean 2:9 3:29, Apocalypse 18:23.†

G3567.def:
νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX: Tob.6:13,16* ;] 
the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Psaumes 19:5, Joël 2:16): Matthieu 22:10 (WE; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Matthieu 9:15, Marc 2:19, Luc 5:34.†

G3568.def:
νῦν, adv., 
[in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה ;] 
__1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opposite to past, Jean 4:18, Actes 7:52, Romains 13:11, 2 Corinthiens 7:9, Colossiens 1:24, al.; opposite to fut., Jean 12:27, Romains 11:31, al.; with art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) and subst., the present: Romains 3:26, Galates 4:25, 1 Timothée 6:17, Tite 2:12, al.; απὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Luc 1:48, Actes 18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Romains 8:22, Philippiens 1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַד עַתָּה), Matthieu 24:21, Marc 13:19; τὰ ν., as regards the present, Actes 5:38; with pret., just now, but now, Matthieu 26:65, Jean 11:8 21:10; with fut., now, presently, Jean 12:31, Actes 20:22; so with praes., presently, forthwith, Jean 12:31 17:13; καὶ ν., Jean 11:22 17:5, al.; ἀλλὰ ν., Luc 22:36; ἔτι ν., 1 Corinthiens 3:2; τότε (πότε) . . . ν. (δέ), Romains 6:21 11:30; ν. ἤδη, 1 Jean 4:3; ν. οὖν, Actes 10:33, al. 
__2. Of logical sequence (often difficult to disting. from the temporal sense; cf. Lft., Notes, 113f.), now, therefore, now, however, as it is: Luc 11:39; καὶ ν., Actes 3:17, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:6, 1 Jean 2:28; id. before δεῦρο, Actes 7:34; ν. δέ, Jean 8:40 9:41 15:22, 24, 18:36, 1 Corinthiens 5:11 7:14 12:20, al. (cf. WM, 579.11).

G3570.def:
νῦνί an Attic strengthened form of νῦν 
(in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : Job 5:1-27, Psaumes 2:1-12, 1-12, 4Ma.4:1-26, Ep. Je* ;] 
now; 
__1. of time: with praes., Actes 24:13, Romains 15:23, 25, 1 Corinthiens 13:13, 2 Corinthiens 8:11 8:22, Phm 9 11; with pf., Romains 3:21; with pret., Romains 6:22 11:30 (WH, mg.) Romains 7:6, Éphésiens 2:13, Colossiens 1:21 3:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, Actes 22:1. 
__2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Romains 7:17, 1 Corinthiens 5:11 (νῦν, WH) 1 Corinthiens 12:18 (νῦν, WH, txt.) 1 Corinthiens 15:20, Hébreux 8:6 (νῦν, WH, txt.), Hébreux 9:26 (cf. WM, 24, 579n).†

G3571.def:
νύξ genitive νυκτός, ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly for לַיִל ;] 
night: Matthieu 12:40, Marc 6:48, Jean 13:30, al.; genitive temp. (of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Matthieu 2:14, Jean 3:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Marc 5:5, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Luc 18:7, Apocalypse 4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Matthieu 25:6; dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν., Luc 12:20, al.; ἐκείνῃ Actes 12:6; ἐπιούσῃ, Actes 23:11; accusative durat. (Bl., § 34, 8; Kühner3, III, 314b), ν. κ. ἠμέραν, Luc 2:37 Actes 20:31; τ. νύκτας, Luc 21:37; διὰ νυκτός (= cl. νυκτός; Bl., § 42, 1; 46, 7), Actes 5:19 16:9 17:10 23:31; δι᾽ ὅλης ν., Luc 5:5; κατὰ μέσον τῆς ν. (Bl., § 47, 6), Actes 27:27. Metaphorical: Jean 9:4, Romains 13:12, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:5

G3572.def:
νύσσω
(Att.. -ττω), [in LXX: Sir.22:19, 3Ma.5:14 * ;] 
to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jean 19:34, [Matthieu 27:49], WH.†

G3573.def:
νυστάζω
(cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc ;] 
to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Matthieu 25:5. Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Psaumes 121:4, Ésaïe 5:27) : 2 Pierre 2:3.†

G3574.def:
νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον
(νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4), 
lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: 2 Corinthiens 11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).†

G3575.def:
Νῶε
(as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ) 
Noah: Matthieu 24:37-38, Luc 3:36 17:26-27 Hébreux 11:7, 1 Pierre 3:20, 2 Pierre 2:5.†

G3576.def:
νωθρός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX: Proverbes 22:29 (חָשֹׁךְ), Sir.4:29 11:12 * ;] 
sluggish, slothful: Hébreux 5:11 6:12 (for similar usage in π., see MM, xvii). 
SYN.: ἀργός (which see), βραδύς

G3577.def:
νῶτος, -ου, ὁ 
in Att.. most frequently τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מֹתֶן ;] 
/the back: Romains 11:10 (LXX).†

G3578.def:
ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(ξένος), [in LXX: Sir.29:27 Bl* ;] 
hospitality, enter­tainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l, but see infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: Actes 28:23, and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l, Phi., p. 9; but see supr., and cf. MM, xvii).†

G3579.def:
ξενίζω
(ξένος), [in LXX: Esther 3:13, Sir.29:25, 2Ma.9:6, 3Ma.7:3 * ;] 
__1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), Actes 10:23 28:7, Hébreux 13:2; pass., Actes 10:6, 18 10:32 21:16. 
__2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: Actes 17:20; pass., 1 Pierre 4:4 4:12.†

G3580.def:
ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω 
(ξένος, δέχομαι), 
to entertain strangers: 1 Timothée 5:10.†

G3582.def:
ξέστης, -ου, ὁ
(a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al. : Lévitique 14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)* ;] 
__1. a sextarius (about a pint). 
__2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone : Marc 7:4.†

G3583.def:
ξηραίνω
(ξηρός), [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ ;] 
to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, Jacques 1:11; pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, Matthieu 13:6 21:19-20, Marc 4:6 11:20-21, Luc 8:6, Jean 15:6, 1 Pierre 1:24; of ripened crops, Apocalypse 14:15; of liquids, Marc 5:20, Apocalypse 16:12; of members of the body, to waste away, Marc 3:1 (cf. 3Ki.13:4) Marc 9:18.†

G3584.def:
ξηρός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה, etc. ;] 
dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., Luc 23:31; of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: Jean 5:3; of the hand, Matthieu 12:10 Marc 3:3, Luc 6:6, 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. Genèse 1:9-10; Jonas 1:19, al.): Matthieu 23:15; γῆ, Hébreux 11:29.†

G3585.def:
ξύλινος, -η, -ον
(ξύλον) [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;] 
wooden: 2 Timothée 2:20, Hébreux 9:20 (cf. Ep. Jérémie 4:1-31 ff).†

G3586.def:
ξύλον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;] 
__1. wood: 1 Corinthiens 3:12, Apocalypse 18:12. 
__2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as, 
__(a) a cudgel, staff: pl., Matthieu 26:47, 55, Marc 14:43, 48, Luc 22:52; 
__(b) stocks, for confining the feet (Job 33:11, סַד) : Actes 16:24; 
__(with) a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet (Deutéronome 21:22-23), in NT, of the Cross: Actes 5:30 10:39 13:29, Galates 3:13, 1 Pierre 2:24. 
__3. In late writers (see MM, xvii), a tree (Genèse 1:29, Ésaïe 14:8, al.) : Luc 23:31; ξ. τῆς ζωῆς, Apocalypse 2:7 22:2, 14 22:19.†

G3587.def:
ξυράω, -ῶ 
late form of ξυρέω (which see) : 1 Corinthiens 11:6 (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but see: ξύρω).†
ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω (Veitch, see word), aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι (Bl., § 24, see word; Zorell, see word, etc.) for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.) : 1 Corinthiens 11:6.†

G3588.def:
ὁ, ἡ, τό, 
the prepositive article (ἄρθρον προτακτικόν), originally a demonstr. pron. (so usually in Hom.), in general corresponding to the Eng. definite article. 
__I. As demonstr. pron. 
__1. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): Actes 17:28 (quoted from the poet Aratus).
__2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other: 1 Corinthiens 7:7, Galates 4:22; pl., Actes 14:4, 17:32, Philippiens 1:16, al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, Matthieu 16:14, Jean 7:12; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, Hébreux 7:21, 23.
__3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he: Matthieu 2:14, Marc 1:45, Luc 8:21, Jean 9:38, al. mult. 
__II. As prepositive article, the, prefixed, 
__1. to nouns unmodified: ὁ θεός, τὸ φῶς, etc.; to abstract nouns, ἡ σοφία, etc., to pl. nouns which indicate a class, οἱ ἀλώπεκες, foxes, Matthieu 8:20, al.; to an individual as representing a class, ὁ ἐργάτης, Luc 10:7; with nom. = voc. in addresses, Matthieu 11:26, Jean 19:3, Jacques 5:1, al.; to things which pertain to one, ἡ χεῖρ, his hand, Marc 3:1; to names of persons well known or already mentioned; usually to names of countries (originally adjectives), ἡ Ἰουδαία, etc.
__2. To modified nouns: with of person(s) pron. genitive, μοῦ, σοῦ, etc.; with poss. pron., ἐμός, σός, etc.; with adj. between the art. and the noun, ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος, Matthieu 12:35; the noun foll, by adj., both with art., ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, Jean 10:11 (on ὁ ὄχλος πολύς, Jean 12:9, see M, Pr., 84); before adjectival phrases, ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις, Romains 9:11. 
__3. To Other parts of speech used as substantives; 
__(a) neuter adjectives: τ. ἀγαθόν, etc.;
__(b) cardinal numerals: ὁ εἶς, οἷ δύο, etc.;
__(with) participles: ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ Βαπτιστής, Matthieu 14:2), Marc 6:14; πᾶς ὁ, with ptcp., every one who, etc.;
__(d) adverbs: τὸ πέραν, τὰ νῦν, ὁ ἔσω ἄνθρωπος;
__(e) infinitives: nom., τὸ θέλειν, Romains 7:18, al.; genitive, τοῦ, after adjectives, ἄξιον τοῦ πορεύεσθαι, 1 Corinthiens 16:4; verbs, ἐλαχεν τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι, Luc 1:9; and frequently in a final sense, ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρειν, Matthieu 13:3 (on the artic. inf., see Bl., §71). 
__4. In the neut. to sentences, phrases or single words treated as a quotation: τὸ Ἐι δύνῃ, Marc 9:23; τὸ ἔτι ἅπαξ, Hébreux 12:27; τὸ ἀνέβη, Éphésiens 4:9, al.
__5. To prepositional phrases: οἱ ἀπὸ Ἰταλίας, Hébreux 13:24; οἱ ἐκ νόμου, Romains 4:14; neut. accusative absol., in adverbial phrases, τὸ καθ᾽ ἡμέραν, daily, Luc 11:3; τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, as regards the flesh, Romains 9:5. 
__6. To nouns in the genitive, denoting kinship, association, etc.: ὁ τοῦ, the son of (unless context indicates a different relationship), Matthieu 10:2, al.; τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, the things that pertain to God, Matthieu 16:23; τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης, Romains 14:19 (cf. M, Pr., 81ff.; Bl, §§46, 47).

G3589.def: eighty , Lat. octoginta, (Thucydides), etc.:—;ionic and doric ὀγδώκοντα, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G3590.def:
ὄγδοος, -η, -ον 
the eighth. Luc 1:59, Actes 7:3" (LXX), Apocalypse 17:11 21:20; one of eight, with seven others (usually, in this sense, with αὐτός added, but cf. Plat., Legg., iii, 695 with; Plut., Pelop., 13; 2Ma.5:27): 2 Pierre 2:5.†

G3591.def:
ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ 
bulk, mass; metaphorically, an encumbrance: Hébreux 12:1.†
SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne

G3592.def:
ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε
(the old demonstr. pron., ὁ + the enclitic δε), = Lat. hicce, this (here), 
referring prop, to what is present, can be seen or pointed out: of a person just named, τῇδε (= ταύτῃ), Luc 10:39; neut. pl., τάδε (λέγει), referring to words which follow (so in Att.., and see MM, xvii) : Actes 21:11, Apocalypse 2:1, 8 2:12, 18 3:1, 7 3:14; εἰς τήνδε τ. πόλιν (= Att.. τῇ καὶ τῇ, Plat., Legg., iv, 721 B), such and such a city, Jacques 4:13.†

G3593.def:
ὁδεύω
(ὁδός), [in LXX : 3Ki.6:12 A (metaphorically, הָלַךְ), Tob.6:5, Wis.5:7 (figuratively)* ;] 
to travel, journey: Luc 10:33 (cf.δι-, συν-οδεύω).†

G3594.def:
ὁδηγέω, -ῶ,
(ὁδηγός) [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ, also for דֶּרֶךְ hi., הָלַךְ hi., etc. ;] 
to lead on one's way, to guide: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 15:14, Luc 6:39; id. before ἐπί, Apocalypse 7:17. Metaphorical, to guide, instruct, teach: Actes 8:31; before εἰς τ. ἀλήθειαν (ἐν τ. ἀ., WH, mg.), Jean 16:13 (cf. Psaumes 25:5).†

G3595.def:
ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX : Esther 8:1, Wis.7:15 18:3, 1Ma.4:2, 2Ma.5:15 * ;] 
a leader on the way, a guide: Actes 1:16. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, Romains 2:19; pl., Matthieu 15:14 23:16, 24.†

G3596.def:
ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ
(ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, Genèse 37:25, al.), 
to travel, journey: Actes 10:9.†

G3597.def:
ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ
(see supr.), [in LXX : Wis.13:18 18:3 19:5, 1Ma.6:41 * ;] 
a journey. Jean 4:6, 2 Corinthiens 11:26.†

G3598.def:
ὁδός, -οῦ, ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for דֶּרֶךְ ;] 
__1. a way, path, road: Matthieu 2:12, Marc 10:46, Luc 3:5 al.; κατὰ τὴν ὁ., Luc 10:4, al.; παρὰ τὴν ὁ., Matthieu 13:4, al.; with genitive of person(s), (subj.), τὴν ὁ. ἑτοιμάζειν (fig.), Matthieu 3:3, Marc 1:3, al.; with genitive term. (obj.), ἐθνῶν, Matthieu 10:5; τ. ἁγίων (figuratively), Hébreux 9:8; accusative, ὁδόν, with force of prep. (like Heb. דֶּרֶךְ; Bl., §34, 8; 35, 5), ὁ. θαλάσσης, Matthieu 4:15 (LXX). 
__2. A traveller's way, journey: ἐν τ. ὁ., Matthieu 5:25, Marc 8:27, al.; ἐξ ὁ., Luc 11:6; εἰς ὁ., Matthieu 10:10; τ. ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι, Actes 8:39; ὁ. ἡμέρας, Luc 2:44; ὁδὸν ποιεῖν (= cl., ὁ. ποιεῖσθαι; V. Field, Notes, 25), to make one's way, i.e. proceed on one's journey, Marc 2:23. 
__3. Metaphorical (cl.; but esp. frequently in Heb.; see Cremer, 442ff.), of a course of conduct, a way of thinking or acting: Actes 14:16, 1 Corinthiens 4:17 12:31, Jacques 1:8 5:20; τοῦ Κάϊν, Ju 11; τ. Βαλαάμ, 2 Pierre 2:15; εἰρήνης, Romains 3:17; ζωῆς, Actes 2:28; ἡ ὁ. ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τ. ζωήν (Dalman, Words, 160), Matthieu 7:14; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Matthieu 21:32; σωτηρίας, Actes 16:17; αἱ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), Actes 13:10, Romains 11:33, Apocalypse 15:3 (cf. Osée 14:9 Psa.94 (95):10, Sir.39:24, al.); ἡ ὁ. τ. θεοῦ (the way approved by God), Matthieu 22:16, Marc 12:14, Luc 20:21; id., of the Christian religion, Actes 18:26; so, absol., ἡ ὁ., Actes 9:2 19:9, 23 24:22; of Christ as the means of approach to God, Jean 14:6. 
__4. Ellipsis of ὁ.: ποίας (sc. ὁδοῦ), Luc 5:19; ἐκείνης, ib. 19:4 (see Bl., §36, 13; 44, 1).

G3599.def:
ὀδούς, -όντος, ὁ 
[in LXX for שֵׁן ;] 
a tooth: Matthieu 5:38, Marc 9:18, Actes 7:54; pl., Apocalypse 9:8, ὁ βρυγμὸς (which see) τ. ὀδόντων, Matthieu 8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luc 13:28.†
